issues.t: Drive motor software can shut off power while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses drive power and coasts, usually with a drivetrain warning on the dash.
issues.why: Software in the electric drive motor controller can wrongly shut down the high-voltage system. BMW recalled about 71,000 electric BMWs for this, including 2022-2025 i4s.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The fix is a free software update, done over the air or at a BMW dealer. If power cuts out, steer to a safe spot and call BMW roadside assistance.

issues.t: "Drivetrain Malfunction" message from a failed charging unit
issues.sym: A "Drivetrain Malfunction" message appears, sometimes with "Driving not possible." The car may refuse to go into drive, stop charging, or lose power, and some owners need a tow.
issues.why: The combined charging unit (CCU), which handles charging and powers the 12-volt system, can be built out of spec and develop an internal coolant leak or insulation fault. BMW issued several service bulletins and delivery stops on 2022-2024 i4s for this part.
issues.next: Have the car towed or driven to a BMW dealer if it will not go into drive. The CCU is a high-voltage part and should be covered by BMW's warranty on a car this new.

issues.t: Battery control software can cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power with a drivetrain or high-voltage warning, sometimes after the car has been parked.
issues.why: Software in the high-voltage battery control unit can interrupt electrical power to the drive system. About 14,000 BMW EVs were recalled.
issues.next: Make sure the free battery control software update has been done. A dealer can confirm it from your VIN.

issues.t: High-voltage battery can short circuit and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Most affected cars show no warning at all. Some may show a high-voltage system warning.
issues.why: A small number of 2022 i4 eDrive40 and M50 batteries could have internal damage that leads to a short circuit and fire risk.
issues.next: If your car is under this recall and has not been fixed, BMW advises not to drive or charge it and to park it outside away from buildings. The dealer replaces the battery free.

issues.t: Battery cell modules may be assembled wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of drive power and a high-voltage warning, though many cars show nothing until a module fails.
issues.why: Some high-voltage battery cell modules may not have been put together properly, which puts stress on the module frame. A failing module can shut down the high-voltage system and raise the risk of fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-470. The dealer replaces the affected modules free.

issues.t: Charging unit may be assembled wrong and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: The car can lose power while driving and may show a drivetrain or charging warning.
issues.why: On a small group of i4 eDrive40 and M50 cars, parts inside the combined charging unit (CCU) may not be connected or assembled correctly.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for this recall. The CCU is replaced free.

issues.t: Battery cell monitoring circuit connections loose (recall)
issues.sym: The car may not start or may shut down, with a message to contact roadside assistance.
issues.why: Electrical connections in the high-voltage battery's cell monitoring circuit may not be secured properly, which can cut power.
issues.next: Check for this recall with your VIN. The dealer replaces the monitoring circuit free.

issues.t: Battery module weld seams can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A high-voltage battery warning may come on. Some cars may show nothing.
issues.why: A few 2024 i4 xDrive40 and M50 battery modules were built with weak weld seams that can overheat and create a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-135. The dealer replaces the battery module free.

issues.t: Left-side body beam may crack (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see or feel. The weakness matters in a crash.
issues.why: The left-side longitudinal beam in the body structure may crack. In a crash, a weakened beam could let the high-voltage battery be damaged, raising the risk of fire.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the beam under recall 24V-611. It is replaced free if needed.

issues.t: Battery cable at rear power distributor can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: The car may stall or lose power. A loose cable can also overheat.
issues.why: The connection between the positive battery cable and the rear power distributor may not be tight, which can cut power or overheat the cable.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-906. The dealer inspects the connection and repairs it free.

issues.t: Whine or grinding from the front electric motor
issues.sym: A growing whine, hum or grinding noise from the front of the car while driving, usually on all-wheel-drive models.
issues.why: BMW found that a bearing in the front electric drive unit can fail because of a manufacturing defect, and put a delivery stop on some cars built in late 2022.
issues.next: Have a dealer listen to the noise and check for bulletin B120522. Repairs on a new car should be covered by warranty.

issues.t: 12-volt battery drains and the car won't wake up
issues.sym: The car is dead or will not switch on after sitting, even though the main battery has charge. Doors may not unlock with the key.
issues.why: A software error can stop the car's computers from going to sleep, so they keep drawing on the small 12-volt battery until it is flat.
issues.next: Jump or charge the 12-volt battery, then have a dealer install the latest software. Replace the 12-volt battery if it has been run flat several times.

issues.t: Car won't charge or doesn't detect the charging cable
issues.sym: Charging will not start on AC or DC chargers, the car doesn't recognize the cable, or the charge light stays white.
issues.why: BMW issued bulletins for charging faults linked to the charging unit and charge-socket electronics. Software and hardware fixes are both used.
issues.next: Try a different charger first to rule out the station. If the car still won't charge, a dealer can run BMW's guided charging test.

issues.t: Coolant leak under the car and weak cabin heat
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the car, a low-coolant warning, and weak heat from the vents, often in very cold weather.
issues.why: The coolant changeover valve in the heat pump system can leak, especially below about 19°F, according to BMW bulletins.
issues.next: Do not keep topping up coolant without finding the leak. Have a dealer check the changeover valve; it is usually a warranty repair.

issues.t: Creaking or knocking when turning the steering wheel
issues.sym: Creaking, cracking or knocking when you turn the wheel while stopped or drive over uneven roads.
issues.why: BMW issued a bulletin for this noise in the steering area.
issues.next: Mention bulletin B320123 to the dealer. It is a noise complaint, not a safety problem, but have the steering checked to be sure.

issues.t: Metallic cracking noise from under the middle of the car
issues.sym: A sharp cracking or metallic noise from under the center of the car.
issues.why: BMW issued a bulletin for this noise from the underbody.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the underbody and battery mounting area and check bulletin B240222.

issues.t: Power windows stop working suddenly
issues.sym: One or more windows stop going up or down without warning.
issues.why: BMW issued a bulletin for sudden power window failures on the i4.
issues.next: If a window is stuck open, cover it to keep rain out and have a dealer check bulletin B510923.

issues.t: Climate control blows the wrong temperature or groans
issues.sym: Poor cooling or heating, different temperatures from left and right vents, or a groaning noise from the middle of the dash.
issues.why: BMW issued bulletins for irregular climate control and for noise from the HVAC unit.
issues.next: Have a dealer check bulletins B640822 and B640422. Software and HVAC parts are usually covered under warranty.

issues.t: Navigation and CarPlay show the wrong location
issues.sym: Maps show the car in the wrong place, navigation keeps rerouting, and Apple CarPlay maps jump around.
issues.why: The car's GPS can send incorrect location data. BMW issued bulletins for wrong GPS position, and owners filed many complaints.
issues.next: Install the latest BMW software update. If it continues, a dealer can check bulletin B841422.

issues.t: Audio cuts out or there is no sound
issues.sym: No sound from radio, phone calls or navigation, or the sound drops out for a while.
issues.why: BMW issued bulletins for audio playback failures, usually fixed with software.
issues.next: Restart the infotainment system. If it keeps happening, ask a dealer for the latest software update.

issues.t: Driver-assist camera switches itself off
issues.sym: Lane keeping, cruise control assist or other camera-based features turn off with a warning message.
issues.why: BMW issued a bulletin for the camera-based driver assistance system deactivating itself.
issues.next: Keep the windshield clean in front of the camera. If the warning returns, have a dealer check bulletin SIB660823.

issues.t: Charge port door won't open
issues.sym: The charging flap stays shut, so you can't plug in.
issues.why: Owners have reported charge port doors that jam. Many were replaced under warranty, but there was no recall.
issues.next: Look in the owner's manual for the manual release for the charge flap. Have the latch replaced under warranty.

issues.t: Doors may not lock automatically after an ECU swap (recall)
issues.sym: The doors don't lock themselves when you drive off.
issues.why: A replacement control module may have been programmed wrong, so automatic door locking does not work as designed.
issues.next: Check for recall 23V-118. The dealer updates the software free.

issues.t: Pedestrian warning sound may not play (recall)
issues.sym: People outside can't hear the car coming at low speeds.
issues.why: The sound generator unit may fault at start-up and not make the required low-speed warning sound.
issues.next: Check for recall 23V-026. The dealer updates the software free.

issues.t: Warnings hidden in Valet Parking Mode (recall)
issues.sym: When Valet Parking Mode is on, important warnings and warning lights may not show on the screen.
issues.why: A software error in the head unit hid critical warnings in that mode.
issues.next: Check for recall 22V-483. The dealer updates the software free.

issues.t: Red airbag warning light stays on
issues.sym: The red airbag light stays on with a restraint system message.
issues.why: BMW issued a bulletin for a restraint system warning that stays on.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read soon. While the light is on the airbags may not work as designed.

issues.t: Black resin leaking from outside door handles
issues.sym: A black, sticky residue drips from under one or more outside door handles.
issues.why: BMW issued a bulletin for resin leaking from the door handle assembly.
issues.next: Clean it off the paint soon and ask a dealer about bulletin B510423; the handle may be replaced under warranty.

issues.t: Moisture inside headlights or taillights
issues.sym: Fog or water droplets inside a headlight or taillight.
issues.why: BMW issued bulletins for condensation inside the lights.
issues.next: Light fog that clears is normal. Standing water or a light that fails should be checked under warranty.

issues.t: Tires wear out fast or car pulls to one side
issues.sym: Tires wear out in a few thousand miles, or the car pulls or drifts to one side even after new tires and an alignment.
issues.why: Owners of 2025 i4s have filed complaints about very fast tire wear and pulling. Dealers point to the car's weight and soft summer tires, but alignment can also be off.
issues.next: Check tire pressures monthly and rotate tires on schedule. If the car pulls, ask for a full alignment and suspension check and keep the records.
